title: Reservations in two countries
summary: MesaLista books tables at 2,000 restaurants in Mexico and Texas. Payments need transactions and favorites are written in both countries.

requirements.1: {{s1}} keeps payments in managed MySQL without leaving Mexico, with a copy in another zone that takes over on its own if the primary fails.
requirements.2: {{s2}} gives reporting a separate copy of the slot 1 primary so it does not slow it down, even if the copy runs a few seconds behind.
requirements.3: {{s3}} stores favorites: each country writes in milliseconds to its own region and both accept writes. The other region sees them later, because availability is preferred over consistency.
requirements.4: {{s4}} alerts the reporting team if the slot 2 copy falls more than 30 seconds behind the primary.
requirements.5: {{s5}} keeps the database password out of the code: the app requests it at startup and a rotation schedule in the same service changes it every 30 days.
requirements.6: The pilot restaurant's MySQL runs on its own premises; its payments are migrated to slot 1 before opening to all 2,000 restaurants.

s1.explanation: With Multi-AZ, RDS for MySQL copies every change synchronously to a standby in another zone, which serves no reads, and if the primary fails RDS switches to the standby on its own. A read replica copies asynchronously and you are the one who promotes it.

s2.explanation: An RDS read replica receives changes asynchronously and serves the reporting queries, so the primary does not carry them even if the copy runs a few seconds behind.

s3.explanation: DynamoDB global tables are multi-active: a change in any replica reaches the others, typically within a second, and by default reads across Regions are eventually consistent.

s4.explanation: RDS publishes the replica lag to CloudWatch as the ReplicaLag metric; a CloudWatch alarm watches that metric against a threshold and notifies the team through SNS when it goes over 30 seconds.

s5.explanation: Secrets Manager keeps the password out of the code and rotates it on a schedule, for example rate(30 days). Parameter Store can point to that secret, but it does not provide automatic rotation for the secrets it stores.

aws-rds-multi-az.s2: The Multi-AZ standby receives the synchronous copy, but unlike a read replica it cannot serve read traffic.

aws-rds-read-replica.s1: The read replica receives changes asynchronously and you are the one who promotes it; it does not replace the primary on its own.

aws-aurora-global.s1: Aurora Global Database copies the data to read-only secondary Regions, and the payments must not leave Mexico.
aws-aurora-global.s2: Aurora Global Database copies an Aurora cluster to other Regions; it is not a copy of the slot 1 MySQL.
aws-aurora-global.s3: In Aurora Global Database only the primary cluster performs writes and the secondary Regions are read-only: there are not two Regions accepting writes.

aws-cloudtrail.s4: CloudTrail records the actions of users, roles and services as events; the lag is the ReplicaLag metric, which RDS publishes to CloudWatch, and the alarm lives there.

aws-parameter-store.s5: Parameter Store stores passwords as parameter values, but it does not provide automatic rotation for the secrets it stores.
